title: A runner's ready mark always arms a wake, and each wake line names the minutes a green PR has sat unmerged (runners 10, 11 and 12)
why: Debt named by runner 10 (09:07 CST Nov 14, relayed), widened by the consultant's 09:07 ask via the coordinator (09:09, relayed; triage read none of it). Two gaps, not one: (1) #2942 green about 16 min unmerged (05:41 to 06:03 CST; runner 10 reported its own session idle then, a gap in its own turns); (2) #3238 (no wake from 08:30 to 09:04; ready run 43604213305 green 08:48:39, merged 09:06:14: 17 min). Runner 10 said at 06:07 it would hold a PR subscription at each ready mark, and the second gap happened anyway (n=2, one runner). Fix shape asked by the consultant: (a) a ready mark always arms a wake, either a PR subscription or a one-time check-in at the run's expected end; (b) each wake line names the minutes a green PR has sat unmerged; (c) scope: runners 10, 11 and 12. Reads: runner 11 named a check-in at each ready mark tonight (#704 ready 07:57, #710 ready 08:40, "check-in in 15 min"); runner 12 unread. The coordinator asked runner 10 why (subscription not set, or set and no wake) and runner 12 the same, and passes the answers. Earlier rescope (coordinator 09:08): root rule git-ci-wait-checks-in already says a session that waits on CI sets a one-time check-in when it starts to wait, so a first fix is a handoff line, not a tool. The consultant's shape adds the second half: the wake line carries the sat-minutes. Whether a tool must arm it, or a handoff line suffices, waits for the answers on why runner 10's subscription did not wake it; if "set and no wake", the cause is in the wake path (a tool or harness fault), not in the runner. Done when: the cause of both gaps is named, runners 10, 11 and 12 each carry the rule, and no green ready run waits over 10 min across the next 5 merges per runner (a count from the merge log; unmeasured now). Folded here, no second record (consultant 09:07).
note: Filed 09:14 CST Nov 14 by triage. Tracker: the coordinator. No lane yet.
